text: By decision of the government, legislative changes will be prepared regarding the recognition of diplomas issued before 2010

By decision of the Government of Georgia, legislative changes will be submitted to Parliament, on the basis of which problems related to the recognition of diplomas issued before 2010 will be resolved for thousands of citizens – the Minister of Education, Science, and Youth of Georgia, Givi Mikanadze, stated.
As the Minister noted, according to the amendment, 4-year full-time and 5-year part-time education will be recognized equally.

According to him/her, the change will affect students who were enrolled in the university in a recognized mode and completed their studies in an unrecognized mode, as well as citizens who were enrolled in the university by educational institutions before obtaining a license.

"We had the following situation – our citizens in 4-year programs were taking exactly the same number of subjects and receiving the same qualification as those in 5-year correspondence programs. According to the legislation existing until now, the 5-year program was equated to a Master's degree, while the 4-year program was awarded a Bachelor's degree. Based on the changes, those who completed a 4-year program will receive a diploma equated to a Master's degree, which will significantly facilitate the employment of citizens in their desired fields."

Before 2010, until a unified system was established, there was no registry in the field of education that ensured students were informed. There were cases when specific universities, which had not been granted accreditation, did not inform applicants about this and enrolled them anyway. Subsequently, when they issued diplomas, graduates faced problems regarding the recognition of this document.

Furthermore, a number of higher educational institutions had authorization for a certain period, which was then terminated during the period of study. Students were not informed about this either, and subsequently, these university graduates faced problems.

“The presented legislative changes will finally put an end to the long, problematic processes that our citizens undergo for the recognition of their diplomas – going to court and appealing processes, which are associated with significant time and effort. All of this will be consigned to history once and for all, and the diplomas of thousands of our citizens will be recognized,” stated Givi Mikanadze.
